title: Redis OOM maxmemory spike killing /auth/v1/token issuance
symptoms: Redis stats: used_memory pinned at maxmemory, evictions climbing
auth-service pod logs: 'OOM command not allowed when used memory > maxmemory'
root_cause: JWT revocation (blacklist) keys were written on every logout/refresh without a TTL, so the set of expired bl_token:* entries grew unbounded. Once Redis hit maxmemory it began refusing writes and evicting live session data, which throttled token issuance.
resolution_runbook: 1. Measure blacklist size: redis-cli -h <redis-host> dbsize && redis-cli -h <redis-host> info memory
2. Purge expired blacklist keys: redis-cli -h <redis-host> --scan --pattern 'bl_token:*' | xargs redis-cli -h <redis-host> del
3. Confirm write headroom restored: redis-cli -h <redis-host> info memory | grep used_memory_human
4. Deploy the fix so new blacklist keys carry a 7-day TTL: kubectl set image deployment/auth-service auth-service=auth-service:v1.8.4 -n production
5. Watch eviction metrics for 30 minutes to confirm no regressions
validation: used_memory fell to 62% of maxmemory, /auth/v1/token p99 back under 300ms, zero OOM errors in 24h.
